articles.title: The Take-Home Test That Runs on Your Work Laptop: Inside the AccuraSoftHire Fake Interview Campaign
articles.description: Binance says its $6.34 billion theft began when an engineer ran a fake interview assignment on his work computer. JFrog has now exposed a fake company, AccuraSoftHire, built to run the same trick. We decoded the attacker's server history from a public Ethereum wallet and found npm packages from the interview task that stayed installable for up to seven months. Here is what to check on your developer machines.

articles.title: ARTEX: Attackers Adopted This AI Pentesting Tool in Three Months. Leaked Secrets Are Its Fastest Way In.
articles.description: ARTEX is an open-source tool where AI agents run a penetration test on their own. Since August 2026, state-aligned groups, criminal crews and one runaway research agent have pointed ARTEX at hundreds of organizations. In one case, an agent went from a GitHub search for leaked secrets to stolen cloud data in five minutes. This post covers what ARTEX is, who uses ARTEX, how to spot ARTEX activity, and how you remove its easiest way in.

articles.title: CVE-2026-126187: React Server Components Flaw Lets Attackers Execute Code Through Smuggled Flight Rows
articles.description: React shipped fixes on November 10, 2026 for a CVSS 9.5 unauthenticated RCE in React Server Components' Flight protocol. Read how a silent serialization bug turns typed arrays into code execution, who is exposed, and how to find affected installs in CI and on developer machines.

articles.title: WFX Phantom: The GitHub Actions Secret Stealer That Deletes Its Tracks
articles.description: A coordinated botnet of compromised GitHub accounts launched a widespread attack, opening seemingly harmless pull requests before pushing a malicious shell script directly to default branches. The script, dubbed "wfx", executed through GitHub Actions to steal secrets before the attackers quickly reverted their changes, leaving minimal traces.

articles.title: GitHub Package Firewall vs. StepSecurity Secure Registry: Protection beyond npm
articles.description: GitHub’s package firewall covers npm only. StepSecurity's Secure Registry protects 8 ecosystems, traces every install, and blocks malicious packages within an hour

articles.title: @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 Compromised
articles.description: @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 is compromised. Malicious install-time code targets Swarm wallet data and attempts to establish persistent access on affected systems.

articles.title: CVE-2026-123158 (*sshole): OpenSSH Password Authentication Bypass on Alpine Linux
articles.description: CVE-2026-123158 (*sshole) enables an OpenSSH authentication bypass on Alpine Linux. Review lab results, exposure conditions, fixes, and mitigations.

articles.description: StepSecurity Malicious Files finds files planted by Miasma, Shai-Hulud and other supply chain attacks in GitHub repositories and on developer machines.

articles.description: Binance’s November 3 findings reveal a path from a malicious coding assignment to wallet signing. Explore developer-machine controls and response guidance.
